stem: We are able to see an object when light from it enters our __________.
solution: We see an object when light coming from it (reflected or emitted) enters our eyes.

stem: The bouncing back of light from a surface is called __________.
solution: Reflection is the return of light after striking a surface.

stem: According to the laws of reflection, the angle of incidence is __________ the angle of reflection.
solution: The law of reflection states that the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection.

stem: The incident ray, the reflected ray, and the normal at the point of incidence all lie in the __________.
solution: By the second law of reflection, the incident ray, reflected ray and normal lie in the same plane.

stem: The line drawn perpendicular to the mirror at the point where light strikes is called the __________.
solution: The normal is the perpendicular to the reflecting surface at the point of incidence.

stem: Reflection from a smooth, polished surface that forms a clear image is called __________ reflection.
solution: Regular reflection from a smooth surface (like a mirror) sends parallel rays in one direction, forming a clear image.

stem: Reflection from a rough surface, which scatters light in different directions, is called __________ reflection.
solution: Diffused (irregular) reflection scatters light in many directions, so no clear image forms; e.g., from paper or a wall.

stem: The image formed by a plane mirror is __________.
options: virtual, erect, of the same size, and laterally inverted
solution: A plane mirror gives a virtual, erect, same-sized image that is laterally inverted.

stem: The left–right reversal in a mirror image is called __________.
solution: Lateral inversion is the apparent interchange of left and right in a plane-mirror image.

stem: When two plane mirrors are placed at an angle, they can form __________ images.
solution: Two mirrors at an angle form multiple images; the number increases as the angle decreases.

stem: A kaleidoscope forms beautiful patterns using __________.
solution: A kaleidoscope uses multiple reflections between mirrors to create changing, symmetric patterns.

stem: The instrument used to view over obstacles (as in a submarine), using two mirrors, is a __________.
solution: A periscope uses two parallel mirrors to see over walls or obstacles.

stem: The transparent front part of the eye that light first passes through is the __________.
solution: The cornea is the transparent front layer of the eye through which light enters.

stem: The coloured part of the eye that controls the size of the pupil is the __________.
solution: The iris is the coloured muscular part that adjusts the pupil size to control the light entering the eye.

stem: The opening in the middle of the iris that allows light into the eye is the __________.
solution: The pupil is the central opening through which light enters the eye; the iris controls its size.

stem: The lens of the eye focuses light onto the __________.
solution: The eye lens focuses incoming light to form an image on the retina at the back of the eye.

stem: The light-sensitive screen at the back of the eye where the image forms is the __________.
solution: The retina is the light-sensitive layer at the back of the eye where the image is formed.

stem: The image formed on the retina is __________.
solution: The eye lens forms a real, inverted image on the retina; the brain interprets it as upright.

stem: The retina sends signals to the brain through the __________.
solution: The optic nerve carries visual signals from the retina to the brain, which interprets them.

stem: The cells on the retina sensitive to bright light and colour are the __________.
solution: Cone cells on the retina are sensitive to bright light and colours; rods are sensitive to dim light.

stem: The cells on the retina sensitive to dim light are the __________.
solution: Rod cells are sensitive to dim light and help us see in low light.

stem: Night blindness, the inability to see well in dim light, is caused by a deficiency of __________.
solution: Vitamin A deficiency causes night blindness; foods rich in vitamin A help prevent it.

stem: The persistence of an image on the retina for a short time after the object is removed is called __________.
solution: The retina retains an image for a fraction of a second (persistence of vision), which is used in cinema.

stem: The splitting of white light into its seven component colours is called __________.
solution: Dispersion is the splitting of white light into its constituent colours, as seen through a prism.

stem: The band of seven colours obtained when white light passes through a prism is a __________.
solution: The spread of colours (VIBGYOR) formed by dispersion is the spectrum.

stem: A rainbow is formed by the __________ of sunlight by water droplets.
solution: Raindrops disperse and internally reflect sunlight, forming a rainbow of colours.

stem: The system of reading and writing for the visually impaired using raised dots is called __________.
solution: Braille uses patterns of raised dots that the visually impaired read by touch.

stem: The Braille system was developed by __________.
solution: Louis Braille developed the Braille system of raised dots for the visually impaired.

stem: To protect our eyes, we should NOT __________.
options: look directly at the Sun or a strong light
solution: Looking directly at the Sun or strong light can damage the eyes and should be avoided.

stem: The number of colours in the spectrum of white light is __________.
solution: White light splits into seven colours: violet, indigo, blue, green, yellow, orange, red (VIBGYOR).

stem: In dim light, the pupil of the eye __________ to allow more light in.
solution: In dim light the iris widens the pupil to let in more light; in bright light it narrows the pupil.

stem: A person who has lost their eyesight can read using the sense of __________.
solution: The visually impaired read Braille by touching the raised dots.

stem: Which of the following is TRUE about a plane mirror image?
options: The image is as far behind the mirror as the object is in front
The image is twice as far behind
The image is on the mirror surface
The image is in front of the mirror
solution: A plane mirror image appears as far behind the mirror as the object is in front of it.

stem: Diffused reflection occurs from a rough surface, but the __________ of reflection are still obeyed at each point.
solution: Even in diffused reflection, the laws of reflection hold at each tiny point; the surface roughness scatters the rays.

stem: The word 'AMBULANCE' is written laterally inverted on vehicles so that it __________.
options: reads correctly in the rear-view mirror of vehicles ahead
solution: It is mirror-written so that drivers ahead see it correctly in their rear-view mirrors.

stem: The muscles that focus the eye lens for near and far objects work by changing the __________ of the lens.
solution: Ciliary muscles change the thickness/curvature of the eye lens to focus on near or distant objects (accommodation).

stem: Which of the following helps keep the eyes healthy?
options: Eating vitamin-A-rich foods and reading in proper light
Rubbing the eyes with dirty hands
solution: A vitamin-A-rich diet and reading in good light protect eye health.

stem: A blind spot exists on the retina where __________.
options: the optic nerve leaves the eye and there are no light-sensitive cells
solution: The blind spot is where the optic nerve leaves the eye; it has no light-sensitive cells, so no image forms there.

stem: White light is a mixture of __________.
solution: White light is a mixture of seven colours, revealed by dispersion through a prism.

stem: The colour of an opaque object we see is the colour it __________.
solution: An opaque object appears the colour of light it reflects; other colours are absorbed.

stem: The two eyes together give us __________ vision, helping us judge distance.
solution: Having two eyes gives three-dimensional (stereoscopic) vision, helping us judge depth and distance.

stem: Reflection that allows us to see non-luminous objects, like a book, occurs because they __________.
options: reflect light falling on them into our eyes
solution: Non-luminous objects reflect light that falls on them; this reflected light reaches our eyes and we see them.

stem: Which of the following instruments uses two mirrors placed parallel to each other?
solution: A periscope uses two parallel mirrors to see over obstacles.

stem: The image in a kaleidoscope keeps changing because __________.
options: the coloured pieces move and are reflected multiple times
solution: As the coloured pieces move, the multiple reflections between mirrors create ever-changing patterns.

stem: Which vitamin is important to prevent night blindness and keep the eyes healthy?
solution: Vitamin A is essential for good vision and prevents night blindness.

stem: When light passes from the object to our eye and forms an image on the retina, the brain __________.
options: interprets the image so we perceive the object upright
solution: Although the retinal image is inverted, the brain interprets it so we perceive the object the right way up.

stem: Which of the following would you use to see a magnified image of a tiny object?
solution: A magnifying glass (convex lens) forms an enlarged image of a small object.

stem: A visually impaired person can be helped in daily life by __________.
options: Braille books, guide sticks and assistance
solution: Braille reading material, walking sticks and human/technological assistance help visually impaired people.

stem: The image formed on the retina of the eye is __________.
solution: The eye lens forms a real, inverted image on the retina, which the brain interprets upright.

stem: The reflecting surface that scatters light in many directions (from a rough surface) causes __________ reflection.
solution: Rough surfaces cause diffused (irregular) reflection, scattering light in many directions.

stem: The overall message of the chapter 'Light' is that:
options: light reflects following definite laws, forms images (as in the eye), and disperses into colours; the eye is a remarkable organ that must be cared for
colours do not exist in white light
solution: The chapter covers reflection and its laws, image formation in mirrors and the eye, dispersion of light, care of the eyes, and reading aids like Braille.

stem: We see objects when light from them enters our __________.
solution: We see when light reflected from objects enters our eyes.

stem: According to the law of reflection, the angle of incidence is __________ the angle of reflection.
solution: The angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection.

stem: The line perpendicular to the mirror at the point of incidence is called the __________.
solution: The normal is the perpendicular line drawn at the point of incidence.

stem: The incident ray, reflected ray and the normal all lie in the __________ plane.
solution: All three lie in the same plane, one of the laws of reflection.

stem: Reflection from a smooth surface giving a clear image is called __________ reflection.
solution: Regular reflection from a smooth surface produces a clear image.

stem: Reflection from a rough surface that does not form a clear image is called __________ reflection.
solution: Diffuse reflection scatters light, so no clear image forms.

stem: The left-right reversal of an image in a plane mirror is called __________.
solution: Lateral inversion is the sideways interchange of an image in a plane mirror.

stem: An image that cannot be obtained on a screen is called a __________ image.
solution: A virtual image only appears to be present and cannot be caught on a screen.

stem: A device that uses two mirrors to see over obstacles is a __________.
solution: A periscope uses two plane mirrors to see over obstacles.

stem: A device that produces beautiful symmetric patterns using mirrors is a __________.
solution: A kaleidoscope uses mirrors to create symmetric patterns.

stem: White light is made up of __________ colours.
solution: White light is composed of seven colours, seen in a rainbow.

stem: The splitting of white light into its component colours is called __________.
solution: Dispersion is the splitting of white light into its spectrum of colours.

stem: The light-sensitive layer at the back of the eye is the __________.
solution: The retina detects the image and sends signals to the brain.

stem: The part of the eye that controls the amount of light entering it is the __________.
solution: The iris controls the size of the pupil and the light entering the eye.

stem: The opening in the eye through which light enters is the __________.
solution: The pupil is the opening through which light enters the eye.

stem: The eye lens focuses light on the retina and is a __________ lens.
solution: The eye lens is a convex lens that focuses images on the retina.

stem: The least distance for clear vision of a normal eye is about __________.
solution: The near point of a normal eye is about 25 cm.

stem: A person who cannot see distant objects clearly has __________.
solution: Myopia makes distant objects appear blurred.

stem: Night blindness is caused by deficiency of vitamin __________.
solution: A lack of vitamin A causes night blindness.

stem: People who cannot distinguish certain colours suffer from __________.
solution: Colour blindness is the inability to distinguish certain colours.

stem: Braille is a system that helps __________ people to read.
solution: Braille is a system of raised dots that visually impaired people read by touch.

stem: A concave mirror is used in a torch to produce a __________ beam of light.
solution: A bulb at the focus of a concave mirror produces a parallel beam of light.

stem: The number of images formed by two mirrors placed at 90° to each other is __________.
solution: Two mirrors at 90° form three images of an object.

stem: As the angle between two mirrors decreases, the number of images formed __________.
solution: Smaller angles between mirrors produce more images.

stem: Objects that give out their own light are called __________.
solution: Luminous objects like the Sun emit their own light.

stem: The Moon is visible because it __________ sunlight.
solution: The Moon is non-luminous and shines by reflecting sunlight.
